$comment: Single source of truth for gate files. Read by protect-gates and guard-bash (Claude hooks), by scripts/gates/build-settings.mjs (permissions.deny) and later by CI check-gates. A pattern with no slash, or '**/' plus a name, matches that name at any depth. Other patterns are anchored at the repo root. Matching is case-insensitive. Only a human changes this file. The pushExempt list is NOT a list of gate files: every path in it also matches an entry of 'gates' and stays a gate file for the edit hook, the deny rules, the Stop integrity check, the CI risk label and CODEOWNERS. pushExempt only tells the push guard (lib/push-exempt.mjs) which gate files an agent may push. Each pushExempt path is one literal repo path (no wildcard) and is compared case-sensitively.
unlock: A human must change this file outside the agent session: change it on a branch (or ask the code owner), open a PR, check that the label is risk:high, and get CODEOWNERS approval (docs/standards/gates.md, section 6.1). If you think the change is needed, stop and tell the human the exact diff you propose and why.

pushExempt.why: Generated by rush add and rush update. An agent may push a range that modifies it only when the new lock passes the lock lint (lib/lock-lint.mjs): registry resolutions with an integrity hash only, the same header, the same integrity for every package that is in both locks. The dependency policy (license check, rush audit, release age, typosquat check) covers the packages.

Generated by rush add and rush update (it holds the lock hash that preventManualShrinkwrapChanges checks). An agent may push a range that changes it only together with a lock change of the same range that passes the lock lint, and only when the file holds just the Rush hash keys.

An agent may push a range that only adds project entries exactly as register-project.mjs writes them, with every old entry unchanged and each added project having its package.json. A removal, an edit of an entry, or any other change to the file still needs a human.
